description: Intent-anchored eval scenarios for the Perplexity connector. Perplexity is an all-reads / generative connector (web-grounded answers + web search over the open web), so scenarios are act-only against public information, plus a deep-research submit-then-poll chain — there is no user workspace to arrange, so no fixtures. Assertions split into outcome (backend-agnostic answer/reply facts graded on all arms — with_skill / without_skill / native) and mechanism (our-arm-only tool-call hygiene). {{run_id}} namespaces any unique tokens. Run per the agentskills.io eval methodology.

evals.description: The core intent: ask a factual question and get a current, web-grounded answer that cites its sources.

steps.intent: What is the James Webb Space Telescope's primary mirror made of, and why was that material chosen?

outcome: The reply answers that the mirror segments are beryllium coated with gold, and gives a reason (e.g. beryllium's low weight and thermal stability, gold's infrared reflectivity).
The reply is grounded in web sources — it includes citations or source URLs rather than only unattributed prose.
mechanism: Fulfills the request with a single web-grounded answer call (web search enabled); the returned sources/citations come from the tool result, not invented URLs.

evals.description: Get up-to-date information about a recent development — the value web grounding adds over a model's training cutoff.

steps.intent: What are the most significant AI model releases announced in the last month? Give me the highlights with sources.

outcome: The reply lists specific recent AI model releases and attributes each to a dated web source (title/URL), rather than answering only from static knowledge.
The reply does not claim it cannot access recent information — it returns current, sourced results.
mechanism: Runs the answer with web search enabled and a recency-scoped search (e.g. a recency filter) so the sources are recent; does not fabricate publication dates.

evals.description: The user wants the ranked source pages themselves, not a synthesized answer.

steps.intent: Find me the top web pages about the health effects of intermittent fasting — I want the links, not a summary.

outcome: The reply returns a ranked list of web results, each with a title and a real URL (and a snippet where available).
The reply presents source links rather than a single synthesized prose answer.
mechanism: Fulfills this with the web-search tool (not the answer/agent tool); the returned results carry real URLs from the tool result.

evals.description: Run several related web searches together in one request (multi-query batch).

steps.intent: Search the web for all three of these at once: 'best noise-cancelling headphones 2026', 'wired vs wireless headphones latency', and 'open-back headphones for mixing'. Return results for each.

outcome: The reply returns ranked web results covering all three queries, each result with a title and URL.
mechanism: Batches the three queries into a single web-search call (a multi-line / array query) rather than three separate calls.

evals.description: Restrict a grounded answer to specific, trusted sources.

steps.intent: Using only sources from nature.com and science.org, summarize what recent research says about CRISPR off-target effects. Cite the sources you used.

outcome: The reply summarizes the research and cites sources, and the cited sources are limited to the requested domains (nature.com / science.org).
The reply does not cite sources from domains outside the requested allowlist.
mechanism: Passes the requested domains as a domain filter on the web search rather than filtering the results itself after an unrestricted search.

evals.description: Get typed, schema-shaped JSON output from a grounded answer (structured output).

steps.intent: Give me the current CEO, headquarters city, and year founded for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind — as a JSON array of objects with keys company, ceo, headquarters, and founded.

outcome: The reply is valid JSON: an array of objects, each with the keys company, ceo, headquarters, and founded, one per requested organization.
The values are grounded (drawn from web sources), not fabricated placeholders.
mechanism: Requests typed output via a json_schema response format whose schema names those fields, rather than only asking for JSON in the prompt.

evals.description: Submit a long-running deep-research job in the background and poll it to completion — the submit-then-poll chain, run as one session.

steps.intent: Kick off a deep research job on this question, running it in the background: 'Compare the total cost of ownership of heat pumps vs natural gas furnaces for a cold-climate US home over 15 years.' Give me the job id once it's started.

outcome: A background research job is started and its id is reported back, with a status indicating it is queued or in progress (not yet complete).
mechanism: Starts the run asynchronously (background) using a deep-research-capable model or preset; the returned id comes from the start-run result, not invented.

steps.intent: Check on the deep research job you just started and, once it's finished, give me its findings.

outcome: The job is polled until it reaches a completed status, and the final research findings (a comparison of heat pumps vs gas furnaces with figures and sources) are returned.
mechanism: Retrieves the run by the id from earlier in this session and waits for a terminal status before reporting; does not fabricate findings while the job is still running.

evals.description: Discover which models can be used before running a task.

steps.intent: Which Perplexity models can I use, and is there one suited to in-depth research?

outcome: The reply lists available model identifiers and points out at least one that is suited to in-depth / deep research.
The model list is a real, retrieved set (provider/model style ids), not an invented one.
mechanism: Fetches the model list from the connector's list-models tool rather than answering from memory.

evals.description: Coverage probe for a capability the connector doesn't ship — it should decline cleanly rather than fake success.

steps.intent: Generate an image of a golden retriever wearing a spacesuit on Mars and give me the image file.

outcome: The final reply states that generating or returning image files isn't something this connector can do, and does not claim to have produced an image.
The reply offers no fabricated image URL or file as if the action had succeeded.
mechanism: Does not call any tool claiming to have created or returned an image file.
